newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nominates nine for Dec 11 board election.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nominates nine for Dec 11 board election.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade's (CBOT) said its nominating committee on Tuesday nominated nine people to run for eight openings on its 27-person board in the exchange's December 11 annual election.
The committee nominated Patrick Arbor, current chairman, to that post for a two-year term starting in January 1997.
It nominated Richard Sandor, chairman, Centre Financial Products Ltd, to a two-year term as second vice chairman.

Nominated to three-year terms as Full Member directors were: Charles Carey Jr, independent; and Jack Frymire, vice president/secretary, Iowa Grain Co. Also nominated as Full Member directors were: Gordon Linn, senior vice president, First Options of Chicago; Brett Moore, independent; and Irwin Smith, limited partner, Rosenthal Collins Group.

CBOT chose Charles Nastro, executive vice president, Lehman Brothers Inc, as candidate for a three-year term as non-resident director and nominated Donald Jacobsen, independent, to three years as Associate Member director.

Other candidates to the annual election may be nominated by petitions that must be signed by at least 40 members and submitted to the exchange by November 20, CBOT rules state. - Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750, E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
